subject: compileNimble error: "Failed to create the shared library"

messages.author: bad39b108b65612c
messages.subject: compileNimble error: "Failed to create the shared library"
parts:
[Note: I've spoken with Chris Paciorek about this offline; he will post a response.]

I've written a nimbleFunction for a user-defined distribution (a multivariate Gaussian with non-full rank precision), but when I try to compile the model code, I get a "Failed to create the shared library" error. Here's the code:

# MV Gaussian with non-full-rank precision 

# Q is an intrinsic CAR precision matrix (MxM) of rank M-1
# Qevecs and Qevals are the eigenvectors/eigenvalues of Q
dmnorm_mdr <- nimbleFunction( # density function
  run = function( x = double(1), mn = double(1), Q = double(2), 
                  Qevecs = double(2), Qevals = double(1),
                  tausq = double(0, default = 1),
                  log = integer(0, default = 0)) {
    
    returnType(double(0))
    
    N <- length(Qevals)
    logDet <- -0.5*(N-1)*log(tausq) + 0.5*sum(log(Qevals[1:(N-1)]))
    logExp <- -0.5*(1/tausq)*t(x - mn)%*%Q%*%(x - mn)
    if(log){ return( -0.5*(N-1)*log(2*3.141593) + logDet + logExp ) }
    else{ return(exp( -0.5*(N-1)*log(2*3.141593) + logDet + logExp )) }
})

rmnorm_mdr <- nimbleFunction( # generate samples from the distribution
  run = function( n = integer(0, default = 1), mn = double(1), Q = double(2),
                  Qevecs = double(2), Qevals = double(1),
                  tausq = double(0, default = 1) ) {
    
    returnType(double(1))
    if(n != 1) print("rmnorm_mdr only allows n = 1; using n = 1.")
    
    N <- length(Qevals)
    z <- rnorm( n = 1, mean = 0, sd = sqrt(tausq/Qevals[1]) )
    y <- z*Qevecs[,1]
    for( i in 2:(N-1)){
      z <- rnorm( n = 1, mean = 0, sd = sqrt(tausq/Qevals[i]) )
      y <- y + z*Qevecs[,i]
    }
    x <- y + mn
    return(x)
})

# Register
registerDistributions( list(dmnorm_mdr = list(
  BUGSdist = "dmnorm_mdr(mn, Q, Qevecs, Qevals, tausq)",
  types = c("value = double(1)", "mn = double(1)", "Q = double(2)", 
            "Qevecs = double(2)", "Qevals = double(1)" ) )))

# Create the model
logit_CAR_code <- nimbleCode({
  # likelihood
  for(i in 1:M) 
    z[i] ~ dbinom(size = N, prob = expit(logit_p[i]))
  # latent process      
  logit_p[1:M] ~ dmnorm_mdr( mn = mn[1:M], Q = Q[1:M, 1:M], 
                             Qevecs = Qevecs[1:M, 1:M], 
                             Qevals = Qevals[1:M], tausq = tausq )
  # process structure
  mn[1:M] <- ones[1:M]*mu
  # hyperparameters
  mu ~ dnorm(0, sd = 100)
  tausq ~ dunif(0, 100)
})
logit_CAR_model <- nimbleModel( 
  code = logit_CAR_code, 
  constants = list(M = M, ones = rep(1,M) ),
  inits = list(mu = 0, tausq = 1, logit_p = rep(0,M) ),
  data = list(z = z, Q = Q, Qevals = Q.evals, Qevecs = Q.evecs, N = N)
)

compl_logit_CAR_model <- compileNimble( logit_CAR_model ) 
# Error: Failed to create the shared library

Thanks-
Mark

messages.author: 5fa2a363d4ddd1d1
messages.subject: Re: compileNimble error: "Failed to create the shared library"
parts:
Thanks, Mark. A couple things here:

1) As of version 6.0 (now on CRAN but not yet on our website as we're
about to go directly to 0.6-1 to fix some logistical issues with 0.6
on CRAN), we are by default suppressing messages from the C++
compiler, so you're not seeing the compiler errors that are occurring
in this case. To see the messages one can do:
nimbleOptions(showCompilerOutput = TRUE)
and then run
compileNimble(dmnorm_mdr)

2) Basically what happens is that NIMBLE tries to compile dmnorm_mdr
(in the process of using the user-defined distribution in your model)
and it has this problem:

g++ -I/usr/share/R/include -DNDEBUG -DEIGEN_MPL2_ONLY=1
-I"/accounts/gen/vis/paciorek/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/3.2/nimble/include"
-Wno-misleading-indentation -Wno-ignored-attributes
-Wno-deprecated-declarations -fpic -g -O2 -fstack-protector
--param=ssp-buffer-size=4 -Wformat -Werror=format-security
-D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=2 -g -c P_2_code_nfCode.cpp -o P_2_code_nfCode.o
P_2_code_nfCode.cpp: In function ‘double rcFun_4(NimArr<1, double>&,
NimArr<1, double>&, NimArr<2, double>&, NimArr<2, double>&, NimArr<1,
double>&, double, int)’:
P_2_code_nfCode.cpp:404:59: error: no match for ‘operator+’ (operand
types are ‘double’ and ‘NimArr<2, double>’)
return(((-(0.5) * (N - 1)) * log(2 * 3.141593) + logDet) + logExp);

^

The issue is that logExp is a 1x1 matrix because it is the result of
matrix computations. But then the your code tries to add that 1x1
matrix to a scalar value. It turns out that it's hard to cleanly
handle cases where higher-dimensional objects are manipulated via
linear algebra calculations and the effective result is a lower
dimensional object, so NIMBLE is finicky about dimensions. And
unfortunately, we're not catching the issue and issuing an error
message. We have some discussion of all this (albeit implicitly) in
Section 9.5.11 of the manual.

In any event, once the issue is recognized, the simple solution is to use
logExp[1,1] in place of logExp when you want to do scalar calculations.
Or you could set logExp to be scalar to start with by doing this:
logExp <- (-0.5*(1/tausq)*t(x - mn)%*%Q%*%(x - mn))[1,1]
